# The lightweight memory engine

> A lightweight external memory engine for small language models running locally on an Apple-silicon Mac (MLX).
> The model reads its memory mostly as its own saved keys and values ("notes"), not as retrieved text: a question
> opens one room of notes on the SSD, read in one burst and laid in front of the model already read, then the four
> closest moments as words. Three layers: a core always in RAM, rooms on the SSD (hot ones kept in RAM), and a vault of
> linked Markdown notes that opens in Obsidian. Python package `camr`; its final name is not chosen yet.

- It is not a vector database. The embedder only chooses which room to open; the model reads the room's notes.
- Everything runs on the Mac. The one outside runtime is Ollama, through a local proxy, where memory goes in as words.
- Python entry points: `camr_engine.memory.Memory` (one folder) and `camr_engine.reach.Session` (several reaches, an on/off
  switch). Both have `remember(text, day, ...)` and `answer(question, today, ...)`. Models: `camr_engine.models.Reader`
  (Qwen3-1.7B 4-bit) and `camr_engine.models.Embedder` (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B).
- Install and run: `sh scripts/install.sh`, then `.venv/bin/python -m camr_engine.app --open` (http://127.0.0.1:8765).
- Benchmark results are kept as dated JSON records under `records/bench/`; the docs point there.

## Docs

- [What it is](docs/site/index.md): the engine in two paragraphs, the page list, and step 1's measurements
- [Quick start](docs/site/quickstart.md): requirements, `scripts/install.sh`, running the app, where files live, troubleshooting
- [The three layers](docs/site/layers.md): the core, the rooms and the vault; how a desk is laid; what a memory folder holds
- [Reach and the switch](docs/site/reach.md): session, project, agent and global memories; reading several, writing one; memory off
- [RAM, the SSD and sleep](docs/site/swapping.md): the tiers, their budgets, sleeping and waking rooms, fading
- [Python library](docs/site/library.md): `Memory`, `Session`, `remember` and `answer` with their real signatures; errands with tools
- [Install and integrate](docs/site/install.md): the `camr` command from curl, uv, pipx, Homebrew or npm; `camr serve`, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with memory (`http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1`, in front of Ollama, LM Studio or mlx_lm.server); configs for OpenCode, LM Studio, Ollama and curl
- [Pairing with Ollama](docs/site/ollama.md): the proxy for the `ollama` CLI (`OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435`), and the macOS app's limits
- [Benchmarks](docs/site/benchmarks.md): the Long Haul, the Hugging Face suites, the Claude yardstick, and the commands to rerun them
- [Metrics](docs/site/metrics.md): what every answer records, and how to summarise it
- [Limits](docs/site/limits.md): what the engine does not do yet
